meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (adv).

meanings.note: Demonstrative pronoun referring to something near the listener or already mentioned. Routinely spoken as 그거. RR: geugeot; spoken geugeo.

meanings.note: Softens a statement or downplays a motive.

meanings.note: Used as connective -고 (꺼놓고).

meanings.en: to end, to finish, to be over
meanings.note: Intransitive verb.

meanings.note: Used as compound noun + -도 (낮잠도).

Where are you going?

meanings.note: Used only with close friends, younger people, or children
Used colloquially for positive or negative emphasis.

examples.trans: The weather is so nice today.
Don't worry too much.

meanings.note: Standard polite affirmative response; also used to acknowledge that one is listening.

examples.trans: Ah, yes.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.trans: I used to play here a lot too.

meanings.en: you have to hang out with me!

examples.trans: With empty hands and just words? Then you have to hang out and play with me!

meanings.note: Used as conditional -면 (덧나면).

examples.text: 안 된다니까, 괜히 돌아다니다가 아픈 데 덧나면 어떡해? 이거 타고 모자 쓰면 사람들이 못 알아본다고.

meanings.note: Common colloquial intensifier in spoken Korean

meanings.en: to be many, numerous, or abundant
